The \emph{spectral norm} $\|\mathbf{M}\|_{2}=\sigma_{\max}(\mathbf{M})$ is the largest singular value; the \emph{nuclear norm} $\|\mathbf{M}\|_{\ast}=\sum_i \sigma_i(\mathbf{M})$ is the sum of singular values. These two norms and rank are reported as mean $\pm$ standard deviation over $20$ seeds. The \emph{median condition number} $\mathrm{med}\,\kappa$ uses $\kappa(\mathbf{M})=\sigma_{\max}(\mathbf{M})/\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{M})$ on realizations with finite $\kappa$.
